source_title: NASA HERC 2027 TEAM BANGLADESH — Rover Mass Calculation
scope: Selected calculation text from the current source mass document. This is a legacy printed-chassis analytical scenario, not a verified current assembled rover mass.
paragraphs: B: Four PETG rims, four TPU tyres and four 6 mm hex couplers
Value we use in our calculation
Rim outer diameter at the tyre seat
Rim barrel inner diameter and width
Tyre carcass outside and inside diameters
Tyre radial body depth before raised tread
Total tyre thickness, rim seat to tread peak
8.5 mm body depth plus 5 mm tread gives 13.5 mm
2.4 mm at each radial and side face
200.2 mm outside, 192.8 mm inside, 85.2 mm wide
Tyre core 15%; raised solid tread 60 cubic centimetres
Rim hub, spokes and bead structure
55 cubic centimetres solid plus 45 cubic centimetres core at 37.5% infill
One brass hex coupler per wheel; 6 mm bore and 30 mm length

We define the 13.5 mm radial tyre thickness as the full body-and-tread depth, not a 13.5 mm solid TPU wall. We model the carcass with the specified skins and lightly filled core. Our analytical wheel dimensions exclude manufacturing fit clearance.
Pi times (188 squared minus 182 squared) times 90 divided by 4000 gives 156.922553 cubic centimetres.
156.922553 plus 55 plus (0.375 times 45) gives 228.797553 cubic centimetres.
Pi times (205 squared minus 188 squared) times 90 divided by 4000 gives 472.252062 cubic centimetres.
Pi times (200.2 squared minus 192.8 squared) times 85.2 divided by 4000 gives 194.604889 cubic centimetres.
277.647173 plus (0.15 times 194.604889) plus 60 gives 366.837906 cubic centimetres.
One wheel and all four wheels
One wheel = 0.2906 + 0.4439 + 0.0186 = 0.7531 kg.Group B = 4 x 0.7531 = 3.0124 kg. We carry forward 3.012 kg.

In our barrel and tyre annular formula, we divide by four for diameters and by 1000 to convert cubic millimetres to cubic centimetres. We count bearings, brackets, spindle hardware and motors in A. 18.6 g coupler specification
C: CF-PLA chassis, suspension structures, complete covering and other body parts

For each part, we multiply 1.21 by the solid volume plus 0.375 times the remaining core volume, then divide by 1000 for kilograms. We keep solid and core regions separate. We treat thin covers and enclosure walls as solid; we leave the enclosure cavity hollow rather than filling it at 37.5%.
550 mm long, 320 mm wide and 8 mm thick; 70% retained after openings. Envelope: 550 times 320 times 8 times 0.70 divided by 1000 gives 985.60 cubic centimetres.
Two 1.2 mm face skins give 295.68 cubic centimetres. Add 96.00 cubic centimetres for retained edges and internal walls: solid 391.68; remaining core 593.92.
Combined member length 1600 mm; 20 mm by 20 mm outer section. Envelope 640.00 cubic centimetres. Equivalent core 11.4 mm by 11.4 mm by 1597.6 mm gives 207.624096 cubic centimetres; solid 432.375904.
Four corner sets, each allocated 70 cubic centimetres solid and 30 cubic centimetres core. Total solid 280; total core 120. Metal pivots and fasteners are already in A.
Developed shell area 0.28 square metres and 3 mm thickness: 2800 square centimetres times 0.30 cm gives 840 cubic centimetres. Includes the outer cover only, not the deck or enclosures.
Two battery enclosures plus two electronics enclosures; combined solid-wall volume 340 cubic centimetres. Straps, cushions, glands and standoffs are in A.
Combined solid volume 200 cubic centimetres and core volume 50 cubic centimetres. Includes camera/LiDAR platform, hood and cradle, display mount, mast and guards; metal fittings are in A.

We use an equivalent shell to model the frame-rail volume; it does not represent a measured extrusion path. Our selected profile gives roughly a 4.3 mm wall; actual perimeter placement depends on the slicer and print orientation. We do not add infill overlap again as a percentage of total mass.
Two battery and two electronics enclosures
We round the displayed values before addition. Our unrounded body calculation gives 3.4465457774 kg and the same 3.447 kg carry-forward value.
We use CF-PLA in place of our earlier 5 kg aluminium stock allowance. We exclude that aluminium stock from the installed rover mass.
We count only finished retained polymer in B or C. We exclude full reels, unused stock, purge, raft and removable support material.
We calculate roughly 1.162 kg PETG for four rims and 1.776 kg TPU for four tyres before printing waste. We therefore need more than our earlier 1 kg PETG stock allowance for the rims alone.
Our CF-PLA body group uses roughly 3.447 kg before printing waste; we budget this material separately from our PETG and TPU wheel stock.
We count metal fasteners, support bearings, couplers, straps and fitted wiring in their assigned A or B rows; we do not add them again in C.
A — Installed task/drive equipment, suspension and metal hardware
B — Four complete wheel assemblies including couplers
C — Printed chassis, covering and other body parts
In pounds: 10.919 divided by 0.45359237 gives roughly 24.07 lb.
20 lb = 9.0718474 kg; nominal excess = 10.919 minus 9.0718474 = 1.8471526 kg, or roughly 1.847 kg (4.07 lb).
Handbook Rule 6.4.5 states a 60 lb maximum. Rule 8.2 awards 5 mass points at 20 lb or less. Our design objective is below 20 lb.

Our theoretical calculation currently exceeds 20 lb. During practical fabrication, we will measure each assembly and try to reduce the mass below 20 lb by refining the chassis, covers, rims and tyre construction while validating their strength. We treat this as our objective, not achieved compliance.
